scenes.vo: In November twenty twenty five, RealPage agreed to pay more than three hundred fifty million dollars over how it priced rent.
For years, landlords across the country fed their private rent numbers into one company's software.

visual.headline:
ONE DATABASE,
THOUSANDS OF LANDLORDS

items.text: Landlords fed in their own private numbers
One shared system saw all of it

visual.source: Source: DOJ v. RealPage antitrust complaint

scenes.vo: Normally, landlords compete by guessing what rivals charge. This software simply told them the real number.
Each night, it sent back a suggested rent for every empty unit, built from its rivals' own numbers.
Regulators say landlords followed the price and left units empty rather than undercut their neighbors.
The Justice Department sued, calling it coordination dressed up as software.

visual.who: Gail Slater, DOJ Antitrust Division · Nov 2025

scenes.vo: When rivals feed their numbers into one piece of software, nobody has to talk to fix the price.

visual.display: When rivals feed their numbers into *one* *piece* of software, nobody has to talk to fix the *price.*
